newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African gold shares closed more than three percent weaker on Wednesday after being knocked by a gold price which breached the psychologically important $350 per ounce level.
The bullion price was fixed at noon $350.10, the lowest since September 15, 1993.
"Gold shares are sharply down tracking the bullion price," a dealer said.
Dealers said investors were discounting gold mine earnings results for the first quarter of the year due to the weak bullion price.
"The market is discounting future earnings from the gold mines. The lower gold price will not benefit them at all," one said.
The gold index lost 40.7 points, or 2.87 points, to end at a new year low of 1,378.2.

Industrial shares regained some of Tuesday's losses on firm world market's led by Wall Street's recovery overnight after Federal Reserve Board chairman Alan Greenspan's comments on the U.S. economy were seen as neutral, dealers said.
Futures players were active in the market and eroded some of the day's gains in late trade.
Overall volumes were fairly large, dealers said.
The industrial index gained 32.7 points to 8,146.6 points and the all-share index rose 18.1 points to 6,756.8 points.
Dealers said the local market would look to movements overnight on Wall Street and in the bullion price for further direction on Thursday.
Freegold lost 175 cents to 32.50 rand, Dries fell a rand to 42.20 rand and Western Deeps shed 800 cents to 130 rand.
First National rose 130 cents to 26.30 rand, Engen gained 80 cents to 28.65 rand and De Beers added 150 cents to 137 rand.
Near-dated industrial equity futures ended firm on a strong Wall Street overnight, but gold contracts mirrored their equity equivalents and fell on the bullion price woes.
The March all-share contract stood at 6,260/70 from 6,243, the industrial contract is at 7,970/83 from 7,931 and the gold contract is at 970/80 from 1,003.
